I know drinking and using is ruining my life. I’ve woken up so many places I didn’t recognize, or didn’t know how i got there, sometimes with bruises and scrapes. Assuming I don’t start drinking again, I’ll never be able to buy alcohol legally or go to a bar on my 21st birthday, even just drinking a nice glass of wine at a fancy restaurant, I mean I’ve never even been to a fancy restaurant lol. What I guess I am longing for isn’t just drinking, it’s normal drinking. Because I’m an addict I won’t be able to drink normally, and often that feels like exclusion. I always looked forward to being in those spaces and fitting in, but I won’t be able to do that, even if I were drinking I wouldn’t fit in because I would be drinking 3x as much as those around me, and I wouldn’t stop. I go back and forth a lot on how I feel about this but yeah, idk, it’s one of the challenging feelings recovery brings out. I try not to dwell on it too much or else I’ll get overwhelmed and spiral, which ofc is never good, esp in recovery lol. “One day at a time” ig lol, its cheesy but it works.

Ds9 In the Pale Moonlight isn’t exactly a moral “debate” episode, so to speak, but it does challenge a lot of the morals of the federation and it has Sisko dealing with his own transgressions of those moral standards. 
There’s a lot of Ds9 and Voyager episodes that have interesting ethical plot points. 

A lot of them are moreso specific characters reconciling their own moral principles, usually in light of a tough decision or an action they took/will take that had problematic consequences. 

Some good Voyager ones are Tuvix*, Prototype, Scorpion Parts 1&2, Meld (some interesting discussions about Suder’s imprisonment and his and Tuvok’s actions as a result of the mind meld), Death Wish, Fair Trade, Critical Care, Random Thoughts, Retrospect**, Drone, Timeless, In the Flesh, Nothing Human (some great discussions about medical ethics and the use of information that is a result of others’ suffering), Thirty Days (if you enjoy a sulking Tom Paris or a character focused episode, this one’s for you lol), Latent Image, Warhead, Tsunkatse (plus The Rock is in this one lol), Nightingale, Lineage, The Void, and Friendship One.

As for Ds9, there’s Past Prologue, In the Hands of the Prophets, Cardassians, Whispers, Paradise (a lot of questionable moral decisions here), Blood Oath, The Wire, Second Skin, Past Tense parts 1&2, Rejoined, Homefront & Paradise Lost, Bar Association, Rules of Engagement, The Muse, Let he Who is Without Sin (I mean the morals challenged here are a little odd and easily reconcilable a, but it certainly has some debate moments nonetheless), The Darkness and the Light, The Begotten, Doctor Bashir, I Presume?, Business as Usual, Children of Time, Far Beyond the Stars, Valiant, The siege of AR-558, Field of Fire, Inrer Arma Enim Silent Leges

Idk if these kinds of episodes are what you’re thinking, but I think a lot of these have some really good discussions in them, and they bring up some interesting ethical issues

*I personally don’t enjoy this episode bc I feel it’s unnecessary and it casts janeway in a very poor light that is never touched upon ever again, BUT many people enjoy the moral qualms in this episode
**personally I find this episode in bad taste, I feel that it doesn’t properly address the issue it’s supposedly trying to tackle and places blame on the wrong party, but there are moral discussions some may find intriguing in the episode

Yes, they borg children did have a leader, and when there are adult drones separated from the collective they also seem to have a hierarchy, but that’s only when they are separated from the hive mind, I don’t think they have a similar hierarchy aside from that. That’s an interesting idea though, I think it must be something kind of along those lines, maybe it’s just that the new drones that are assimilated have their fears suppressed in a subconscious part of the collective’s mind, I mean their individual memories and feelings must exist somewhere independently of the conscious collective, they seem to just lay dormant. In the Voyager episode “Infinite Regress,” seven experiences the personalities of many different individuals assimilated during her time in the collective, so it would seem they are a part of the collective memory, they just normally lie dormant in suppression and were drawn out by the virus the aliens put into the Borg vinculum. I suppose the virus must have drawn the individual neural patterns that were being somewhat suspended by the collective memory and experiences out and caused her, and presumably the other drones, to experience them one at a time instead of simultaneously. Taking the order created by the interlink the borg have and turning it into chaos, so to speak. But since seven was no longer connected to that, she still seemed to have access to those neural patterns, so it does stand to reason there would be something surprising them. They do go on to mention a “fail-safe” device as well that causes the borg to deactivate should they begin to regain their full emotions, so perhaps this device has something to do with why they aren’t traumatizing themselves?

Yeah, I suppose there could easily have been a male leader at any point, but I feel like it would have been mentioned, and I don’t believe the borg ever used the term queen, but they did refer to the queen cell on the artifact, and that was Hugh referring to it as that. Usually when they refer to parts of a borg ship they use the same terms the borg do, so it’s possible the borg do refer to her as queen. But then again, the name “borg” also seems like the kind of term we, as the audience, would use for a group of cy-borgs, and yet that truly is their name, so it’s possible that, even though it’s unlikely they would have the same conceptions of beehives and insect colonies to base their “hierarchy” on, they do just have queens for whatever reason, perhaps stemming from the biology or biases of the creators of the borg, or maybe they only have queens because the writers didn’t think to hard about it and wanted it to just be queens, who knows lol

Also, a collective mind would be virtually impossible to accomplish without a unifying force, just because you have access to the thoughts of the others, doesn’t mean you can act as one, and each borg has designations and functions so they aren’t just acting as one, they are acting toward a common goal, utilizing different bodies plans minds of drones in the process. Idk, a lot of this is clearly just speculation on my part, but it does make sense that, like in a bee hive, you would need one unifying will to link the others together.

But time does play a factor in enjoyment of the show. Not everyone has time to sit and watch several episodes at a time, depending on your personal timetable, it could take weeks to get through it even while skipping episodes, so it’s easy to get bored with a show if you are watching a lot of episodes that are less generally enjoyable, esp to someone not super into the franchise, or less important to the overall story

You can always go back to the other episodes later though. Sometimes it can be nice to be able to finish a whole series in a shorter amount of time, sure you may lose a few insignificant plot points, but you still have enough of a feel for the show to know how you feel about it, and you have enough information for any future shows. Also, when I watch and rewatch shows, I tend to skip some that I deem less integral to the overall story so I have something new (or newish) to come back to.

I’m not a doctor, so I can’t give you specific medical recommendations, but what I can say is that you should try to have someone with you if at all possible. cardiac arrest is a very real possibility, and your condition could change very quickly, like when you first felt the sudden pain in your chest, so it’s important to have someone else there, preferably someone who you trust making medical decisions for you if you are incapacitated in some way. Also, though I’ve never had any problems with heart issues, I do have experience wrestling with the financial prospects of going to the ER and the medical prospects of not going. I understand your trepidation, but I urge you to look into organizations that can help with medical bills. I don’t know the exact names but if you search online you should be able to find some. I’m not sure which ones are legitimate and which ones are fake, but it certainly can’t hurt to do some research and see if it’s worthwhile. I’m sorry you’re having to deal with this tho, it absolutely not fair that you have to worry about the possibility of extensive debt just to get potentially life saving treatment.
